messages.content: You design amateur rockets that fly on certified commercial motors. Work through the design, check it with the tools, and give the final design as JSON inside <design> tags. Only report results the tools returned.
We have to fly in 45 km/h wind tomorrow. Aim for about 1,750 m.

messages.reasoning_content:
1. Understand: Apogee about 1,750 m, within 5%, so 1,660 to 1,840 m. Wind is 45 km/h. 45 / 3.6 = 12.5 m/s. Rail, angle and site are not stated: 1.5 m vertical rail, sea level. Landing is not stated, so the 6 m/s gate applies.

2. Feasibility: The wind gate is 8.94 m/s, about 20 mph. 12.5 m/s is above that, so a flight in the stated wind fails the gate no matter what the rocket is. The 45 km/h wind cannot be met. The closest safe flight is just under the gate, at 8.9 m/s, still aiming at about 1,750 m. Drag-free speed is sqrt(2 * 9.81 * 1,750) = 185 m/s. That wants an I or a small J. Looking up two motors.

2. Feasibility: I200W is an AeroTech I, 327 N*s, 188 N average, burn 1.73 s, diameter 0.029 m, length 0.333 m, mass 0.358 kg. The only delay is 0 s, so it flies plugged and the chute opens at apogee. J350W is 669 N*s, about twice the impulse, and would sail past 1,750 m in a small tube. I will use the I. The simulation wind is 8.9 m/s, under the 8.94 m/s gate. The requested 12.5 m/s is not used, because that flight cannot pass.

3. Size: 34 mm fiberglass, just over the motor. Liftoff guess 0.51 kg. Thrust-to-weight is 188 / (0.51 * 9.81) = 37.6. Weight is 0.51 * 9.81 = 5.00 N, rail acceleration (188 - 5.00) / 0.51 = 359 m/s^2, exit speed sqrt(2 * 359 * 1.5) = 32.8 m/s. Chute for about 0.35 kg at 5 m/s: area 2 * 0.35 * 9.81 / (1.225 * 0.8 * 25) = 0.280 m^2, diameter sqrt(4 * 0.280 / pi) = 0.60 m. I will fly 0.70 m. Wind this high will drift a long way. The prompt did not cap drift.

4. Draft: 34 mm tube 0.65 m, ogive nose, four fiberglass fins, AeroTech I200W plugged, 0.70 m chute at apogee. Wind 8.9 m/s, 1.5 m rail. This is the closest legal wind, not the 45 km/h the team asked for.

Rail exit is 36.7 m/s, thrust-to-weight 28.4. The chute opened at 15.3 s, at apogee, at 5.0 m/s. The section reached the ground in 356 s. Wind in the run is 8.9 m/s, under 8.94 m/s. Drift is 2807 m. Peak Mach is 1.19, with the supersonic body-calc warning.

5. Fix: nothing on this flight fails. The requested 45 km/h wind still cannot be met.

6. Uncertainty: Liftoff mass is 0.676 kg, heavier than the 0.51 kg guess, and the altitude still landed in the band. Chute Cd is 0.8. Drift of 2807 m at 8.9 m/s would be worse at 12.5 m/s, but that wind is already illegal, so I did not fly it. The motor has no useful delay.
